studies.Reference: Variation of urinary and serum trace elements (Ca, Zn, Cu, Se) in bladder carcinoma in China.
studies.Title: Variation of urinary and serum trace elements (Ca, Zn, Cu, Se) in bladder carcinoma in China.
studies.Authors: Guo KF, Zhang Z, Wang JY, Gao SL, Liu J, Zhan B, Chen ZP, Kong CZ
studies.Journal: Asian Pacific journal of cancer prevention : APJCP
studies.Population: Patients with bladder carcinoma and healthy persons in China
studies.comparison_type: cases versus healthy controls (serum and urinary copper levels)

sample_size.excerpt: To determine this, 81 patients with bladder carcinoma chosen as a study group and 130 healthy persons chosen as a control group were all assayed for urinary and serum trace elements (calcium [Ca], zinc [Zn], copper [Cu], selenium [Se]) using an atomic absorption spectrophotometer, and the results were analyzed by independent sample t tests.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 81 + 130 = 211

cases.excerpt: Since there are few studies of the effect of trace elements in bladder carcinoma in China, the aim of this study was thus to assess variation using a case control approach. To determine this, 81 patients with bladder carcinoma chosen as a study group and 130 healthy persons chosen as a control group were all assayed for urinary and serum trace elements (calcium [Ca], zinc [Zn], copper [Cu], selenium [Se]) using an atomic absorption spectrophotometer, and the results were analyzed by independent sample t tests.

comparison.excerpt: There were higher urinary Zn and serum Cu concentrations in bladder carcinoma cases.

design.excerpt: the aim of this study was thus to assess variation using a case control approach

timing.excerpt: were all assayed for urinary and serum trace elements

exposure_measurement.excerpt: assayed for urinary and serum trace elements (calcium [Ca], zinc [Zn], copper [Cu], selenium [Se]) using an atomic absorption spectrophotometer

studies.Reference: Copper and zinc levels in plasma and cancerous tissues and their relation with expression of VEGF and HIF-1 in the pathogenesis of muscle invasive urothelial bladder cancer: a case-controlled clinical study.
studies.Title: Copper and zinc levels in plasma and cancerous tissues and their relation with expression of VEGF and HIF-1 in the pathogenesis of muscle invasive urothelial bladder cancer: a case-controlled clinical study.
studies.Authors: Mortada WI, Awadalla A, Khater S, Ahmed A, Hamam ET, El-Zayat M, Shokeir AA
studies.Journal: Environmental science and pollution research international
studies.Population: Transitional bladder cell carcinoma patients and matched controls
studies.comparison_type: Bladder cancer patients versus matched controls (plasma Cu levels; logistic regression)

sample_size.excerpt: Plasma levels of Cu and Zn were determined in 66 transitional bladder cell carcinoma patients (BC group) and 60 matched controls.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 66 + 60 = 126

cases.excerpt: To evaluate Cu and Zn levels in bladder cancer (BC) patients and their relationship with expression of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and hypoxia-inducible factor 1 (HIF-1). Plasma levels of Cu and Zn were determined in 66 transitional bladder cell carcinoma patients (BC group) and 60 matched controls.

comparison.excerpt: Logistic regression analysis revealed that the increase in plasma Cu/Zn ratio and plasma Cu and the decrease in plasma Zn may be risk factors for development of bladder cancer.

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Plasma levels of Cu and Zn were determined in 66 transitional bladder cell carcinoma patients (BC group) and 60 matched controls.
